text.en: On a clear night Raju saw a milky band across the sky. "That is our galaxy, the Milky Way," said his grandfather.

The universe is believed to have begun about 13.7 billion years ago with a huge explosion, the Big Bang. The part we can observe is called the observable universe. Stars are grouped in galaxies, and our galaxy is the Milky Way, so named because it appears as a milky band of light. Groups of stars that form patterns are constellations.
The solar system has the Sun at the centre, which is a star, with eight planets going round it along paths called orbits. The time for one revolution is the period of revolution and the time for one rotation is the period of rotation. The four inner planets are rocky or terrestrial, and the four outer planets, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, are gas giants.
Other bodies of the solar system are moons, asteroids, comets and meteors. Kepler's laws describe how planets move around the Sun, and an object orbiting the Earth needs a certain orbital velocity. The International Space Station is a laboratory in orbit built by many nations working together.

prompt.en: A friend says The Earth is at the centre of the universe. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Early people thought so before telescopes.
The Earth is one planet going round the Sun, in one galaxy among many.
